_style: Address the user always with respectful “আপুনি” (আপোনাৰ, আপোনাক, আপোনালৈ) and the matching polite imperative in -ক/-ওক (সংৰক্ষণ কৰক, পঠিয়াওক, চেষ্টা কৰক); never তুমি/তই towards the user. The couple together is “আপোনালোক দুয়ো” / “আপোনালোকৰ” or simply “দুয়ো”, “একেলগে” (“your story” → “আপোনালোক দুয়োৰে কাহিনী”). The other person is always “আপোনাৰ সংগী” (or “সংগী” alone in labels), never স্বামী/পত্নী, প্ৰেমিক/প্ৰেমিকা, বন্ধু/বান্ধৱী; Assamese verbs carry no gender, so keep it that way: avoid gendered nouns and adjectives and use neutral words (মানুহজন, সংগী, দুয়ো). Exception: preset messages, reactions and pings that the user sends in their own voice to the partner use intimate “তুমি” (“তোমাক মনত পৰিছে”, “ফোন কৰা”). Quote marks: curly “ ” outside, ‘ ’ inside, only where the English has quotes; end sentences with the Assamese দাড়ি “।” (not a Latin period), with ? and ! directly attached (no space before ? ! : ;); single-character ellipsis “…”; keep the dash — with spaces, the “·” separator, emoji, “Coupley”, “Premium” and “AI” in Latin script. Never hard-code numbers or dates: keep every %lld, %d, %@ placeholder intact and let iOS format numbers and dates (Assamese digits ০–৯, day-month-year order, e.g. ১৪ নৱেম্বৰ ২০২৬); if a literal number must appear in text, write it in Assamese digits. Assamese has no letter case: titles, tabs and buttons are short noun phrases or a short polite imperative (“সংৰক্ষণ কৰক”, “চিঠি পঠিয়াওক”, “পুনৰ চেষ্টা কৰক”), no trailing দাড়ি on buttons, chips, tabs or titles. Script: write genuine Assamese orthography, never Bengali spellings: ৰ (not র) and ৱ (not ব for /w/), ক্ষ, the apostrophe for the o-sound (হ'ল, ক'ড, প্ৰ'ফাইল, ব'ৰ্ড); loanwords in Assamese spelling (ছেটিংছ, ৱিজেট, একাউণ্ট, কুইজ). Plural categories are ["one","other"]: after a numeral Assamese uses a classifier (-টা, -জন, -খন) or a bare noun without a plural suffix (-বোৰ/-সমূহ), so “one” and “other” normally carry the same text (“%lld দিন”, “%lld টা স্মৃতি”). A partner's name placeholder (%@) is never declined: never glue a case suffix to it (no %@ৰ, %@ক, %@লৈ, %@ত, %@য়ে); rephrase so the name stands bare, as the subject or after a colon (“চিঠি পঠিয়াইছে: %@”, “নতুন সংগী: %@”), and put any case ending on a neighbouring noun instead of on the name. Tone: warm, gentle, modern everyday Assamese, never flowery or cheesy.
